newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to spend $625 million on engines.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to spend $625 million on engines.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said it will spend $625 million to introduce a new family of all-aluminum V-6 engines over the next two years.

Chrysler said the new engines, which will power its next generation 1998 Dodge Intrepid, Chrysler Concorde, Chrysler LHS and Eagle Vision cars, are 10 percent more fuel efficient and 25 percent more powerful than the engines they replace.
Much of the investments will go to upgrade the plants that will build the engines, in Kenosha, Wis., and Trenton, Mich.
Kenosha will build about 400,000 2.7-liter engines annually, while Trenton will produce about 240,000 3.2-liter and 3.5 liter engines annually.

The Kenosha-made dual overhead cam engines, which produce 200 horsepower, will replace the cast-iron 3.3-liter V6 as the base engine in the Intrepid and Concorde. They also will be used in other Chrysler vehicles, a company spokesman said.
The engines were developed in 24 months, much shorter than the five-year development time for many other engine programs, which often approach investments of $1 billion.
The 220-horsepower 3.2-liter engine will power the Concorde LXI and Intrepid ES models, while the 250-horsepower 3.5-liter engine will appear in the Chrysler LHS and Eagle Vision cars.
Volume production of the engines will begin in August 1997.
